question: Which of the following pairs of an Indus Valley Civilisation site and its present-day location is correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalibangan - Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalibangan is situated in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, on the banks of the dried-up Ghaggar (Saraswati) river. Its name means "black bangles". (कालीबंगा — राजस्थान)

 

• Kalibangan is famous for the discovery of the world's earliest attested ploughed field, fire altars suggesting ritual practice, a wooden furrow, and evidence of an earthquake. It was excavated by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar.

 

• The correct locations of the other major Harappan sites:

◦ Harappa — Montgomery district, Punjab (Pakistan), on the Ravi; excavated by Daya Ram Sahni, 1921

◦ Mohenjodaro — Larkana district, Sindh (Pakistan), on the Indus; excavated by R.D. Banerji, 1922; site of the Great Bath and the Great Granary

◦ Lothal — Gujarat, on the Bhogava river; famous for its dockyard, the earliest known in the world

◦ Dholavira — Gujarat, in the Rann of Kachchh; noted for its three-part division and water-harvesting reservoirs; a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021)

◦ Rakhigarhi — Haryana, the largest Harappan site in India

◦ Banawali and Bhirrana — Haryana; Ropar (Rupnagar) — Punjab, India; Alamgirpur — Uttar Pradesh, the easternmost site

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indus Valley Civilisation flourished about 2500-1750 BCE and is also called the Harappan Civilisation, after the first site excavated. It belongs to the Bronze Age, and its people did not know the use of iron.

 

• The civilisation is noted for its town planning on the grid pattern, burnt-brick buildings, an elaborate drainage system, standardised weights and measures in multiples of 16, and a pictographic script written in the boustrophedon manner, which remains undeciphered.

 

NOTE

 

• Lothal (Option 1): Located in Gujarat, not Punjab; it was the port town of the civilisation.

 

• Dholavira (Option 3): Located in Gujarat, not Haryana.

 

• Rakhigarhi (Option 4): Located in Haryana, not Uttar Pradesh.

question: The Chapchar Kut festival of Mizoram is celebrated to mark which of the following?
option_1: The completion of the clearing of forest patches for jhum cultivation, before sowing begins
option_2: The harvest of paddy at the close of the monsoon
option_3: The Mizo new year, observed in January
option_4: A ceremony held in memory of departed ancestors
solution_text:
The correct answer is The completion of the clearing of forest patches for jhum cultivation, before sowing begins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chapchar Kut is the most important and most popular festival of Mizoram, celebrated in March after the work of clearing the jungle for jhum (shifting) cultivation has been finished, and before the sowing begins. It is thus a spring festival of leisure between two phases of hard labour. (चपचार कुट — मिज़ोरम)

 

• Its high point is the Cheraw, the bamboo dance, in which dancers step nimbly between long bamboo staves beaten together in rhythm. Men and women perform in traditional costume to the accompaniment of drums and gongs.

 

• Mizoram observes three Kuts:

◦ Chapchar Kut — March, after jhum clearing

◦ Mim Kut — August-September, the maize festival, also held in memory of the departed

◦ Pawl Kut — December, the harvest festival

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jhum (shifting) cultivation is practised widely in the North East: a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, cropped for two or three years, and then left fallow to recover. It is known by different names — Podu in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, Bewar and Dahiya in Madhya Pradesh, Kumari in the Western Ghats and Khil in the Himalayas.

 

• Other festivals of the North East: Nyokum of the Nyishi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, in which "Nyok" means land or earth and "Kum" means collectiveness, so that the festival signifies the coming together of people and the earth; Wangala of the Garos; Hornbill of Nagaland; and Bihu of Assam.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The harvest festival of Mizoram is Pawl Kut, held in December.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Chapchar Kut falls in March, and is not a new-year observance.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: It is Mim Kut that carries a commemorative element for the departed.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

A raga which uses all the seven notes in both its ascent and descent is classified under the ______ jaati.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sampoorna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Indian classical music, ragas are classified into jaatis according to the number of notes (swaras) they employ: (राग की जातियाँ — स्वरों की संख्या के आधार पर)

◦ Audav — five notes (pentatonic)

◦ Shadav — six notes (hexatonic)

◦ Sampoorna — all seven notes (heptatonic)

 

• A raga must use a minimum of five notes; no raga may have fewer. The classification is applied separately to the aroha (ascent) and the avaroha (descent), so that a raga may be, for example, Audav-Sampoorna — five notes going up and seven coming down.

 

• The seven basic swaras are Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni — Shadaja, Rishabha, Gandhara, Madhyama, Panchama, Dhaivata and Nishada. Sa and Pa are achal (fixed) notes and are never altered; the remaining five are variable.

 

• Raga Bhupali and Raga Malkauns are classic examples of Audav ragas; Raga Yaman and Raga Bilawal are Sampoorna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Every raga has a vadi (the most prominent note), a samvadi (the second most prominent), anuvadi (consonant notes) and vivadi (dissonant notes), and is associated with a particular time of day or season.

 

• Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande classified Hindustani ragas into ten thaats, while Venkatamakhi devised the 72 Melakarta scheme for Carnatic ragas.

 

NOTE

 

• Audav (Option 1): A raga using five notes.

 

• Shadav (Option 2): A raga using six notes.

 

• Vakra (Option 4): Not a jaati at all — vakra describes a crooked or zig-zag movement of notes within a raga, where the notes do not proceed in strict order.

question: Which of the following statements about the game of football is correct?
option_1: A throw-in may lawfully be taken with one hand
option_2: The goalkeeper may handle a ball deliberately kicked back to him by a team-mate
option_3: A player who is shown two yellow cards in the same match is then shown a red card and sent off
option_4: A match consists of four quarters of twenty minutes each
solution_text:
The correct answer is A player who is shown two yellow cards in the same match is then shown a red card and sent off.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In football, a yellow card is a caution. A player who receives a second yellow card in the same match is shown a red card and is sent off, and the team must continue with ten players, since the player cannot be replaced. (फुटबॉल — दो पीले कार्ड के बाद लाल कार्ड)

 

• A direct red card may also be shown straightaway for serious foul play, violent conduct, spitting, or denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by a deliberate handball.

 

• Basic rules of the game: a match consists of two halves of 45 minutes, with a 15-minute interval; each side fields eleven players including a goalkeeper; and the offside rule applies in the opponent's half.

 

• A throw-in must be taken with both hands, from behind and over the head, with both feet on or behind the touchline and in contact with the ground.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The world governing body is FIFA, founded in 1904 and headquartered at Zurich, Switzerland. The FIFA World Cup has been held since 1930, when Uruguay won the first edition.

 

• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) was founded in 1937. India's premier domestic competitions are the Indian Super League, the I-League, the Santosh Trophy and the Durand Cup, the last being Asia's oldest football tournament.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: A throw-in taken with one hand is a foul throw, and possession passes to the opposing side.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Under the back-pass rule, introduced in 1992, a goalkeeper may not handle a ball deliberately kicked to him by a team-mate; the penalty is an indirect free kick.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Football is played in two halves of 45 minutes; four quarters is the format of basketball.

question: At which edition of the Olympic Games did India win its first ever gold medal in hockey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amsterdam 1928.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey at the Amsterdam Olympics of 1928, defeating the Netherlands 3-0 in the final. The team, led by Jaipal Singh Munda as captain, did not concede a single goal in the entire tournament. (एम्स्टर्डम 1928 — भारत का पहला हॉकी स्वर्ण)

 

• Dhyan Chand was the top scorer of that tournament and went on to become the greatest name in Indian hockey, winning three Olympic golds — 1928, 1932 and 1936. He is called "The Wizard" or "The Magician" of hockey, and his birthday, 29 August, is observed as National Sports Day.

 

• India won six consecutive Olympic hockey golds from 1928 to 1956, and eight in all, the last coming at Moscow in 1980. After a gap of 41 years, India won bronze at Tokyo 2020 and again at Paris 2024.

 

• At the Los Angeles Olympics of 1932, India defeated the United States 24-1, still a record margin; Roop Singh, the younger brother of Dhyan Chand, scored 10 goals in that match and Dhyan Chand scored 8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hockey India is the national governing body, and the international federation is the FIH, headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• Other legendary Indian hockey players include Balbir Singh Sr., who won three Olympic golds and scored five goals in the 1952 final, Leslie Claudius, K.D. Singh Babu and Ajit Pal Singh, captain of the side that won the 1975 World Cup at Kuala Lumpur — India's only hockey World Cup title.

 

NOTE

 

• Los Angeles 1932 (Option 1) and Berlin 1936 (Option 2): India won gold at both, but these came after the first gold of 1928.

 

• London 1948 (Option 3): India's first Olympic gold as an independent nation, won by defeating Great Britain 4-0 — but not the country's first hockey gold.

question: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 during India's presidency of which grouping?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The G20.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA) was launched on 9 September 2023 at the G20 Summit in New Delhi, during India's G20 presidency. (वैश्विक जैव ईंधन गठबंधन — जी20 शिखर सम्मेलन, नई दिल्ली, 2023)

 

• Its founding members include India, the United States and Brazil, which together account for the bulk of world ethanol production and consumption. The Alliance seeks to accelerate the global uptake of biofuels, facilitate technology transfer, develop standards and certification, and strengthen trade in biofuels.

 

• The theme of India's G20 presidency was "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — One Earth, One Family, One Future". Two other major outcomes of the New Delhi Summit were the admission of the African Union as a permanent member of the G20, and the announcement of the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC).

 

• India has advanced its own Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, achieving the target of 20 per cent ethanol blending ahead of schedule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The G20 was formed in 1999 at the level of finance ministers and was raised to a leaders' summit in 2008 after the global financial crisis. It has no permanent secretariat, and works through a rotating presidency supported by the troika of the past, present and future presidencies.

 

• Other groupings and their India-linked initiatives: the International Solar Alliance, co-founded by India and France in 2015 at COP21; the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), launched by India in 2019; and the BRICS Startup Forum, launched in 2021 under India's BRICS presidency to promote cross-border startup collaboration.

 

NOTE

 

• BRICS (Option 2): India's 2021 BRICS presidency produced the BRICS Startup Forum, not the Global Biofuels Alliance.

 

• The SCO (Option 3): India hosted the SCO Summit in 2023, but the biofuels alliance was not an SCO initiative.

 

• ASEAN (Option 4): India is a dialogue partner of ASEAN, not a member, and cannot hold its chairmanship.

question:
Which statements about 'Playing It My Way' are correct?

1) It is the autobiography of the cricketer Sachin Tendulkar.

2) It was co-written with the sports historian and journalist Boria Majumdar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. 'Playing It My Way' (2014) is the autobiography of Sachin Tendulkar, published shortly after his retirement from international cricket in November 2013. (प्लेइंग इट माई वे — सचिन तेंदुलकर की आत्मकथा)

 

• It was co-written with Boria Majumdar, a well-known sports historian and journalist, and traces Tendulkar's career from his boyhood under coach Ramakant Achrekar to his 200th and final Test match at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.

 

• Sachin Tendulkar is the only cricketer to have scored 100 international centuries and the first to score a double century in a One Day International. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2014, becoming the first sportsperson and the youngest recipient of the honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known sports books and their subjects:

◦ 'The Race of My Life' — Milkha Singh, with Sonia Sanwalka

◦ 'Unbreakable' — Mary Kom

◦ 'Ace Against Odds' — Sania Mirza

◦ 'Straight from the Heart' — Kapil Dev

◦ 'A Century is Not Enough' — Sourav Ganguly

◦ 'The Neeraj Chopra Story: The Man Who Made History' — an account of Neeraj Chopra's training, mindset and challenges, written by Norris Pritam, a veteran sports journalist, and not by his coach

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.

question: An alluvial fan is typically formed under which of the following conditions?
option_1: Where a river descends abruptly from a steep mountain slope onto a plain and deposits its load
option_2: Where a river enters the sea and builds up a triangular deposit at its mouth
option_3: Where wind piles up sand at the foot of a desert dune
option_4: Where a glacier deposits unsorted till at its snout
solution_text:
The correct answer is Where a river descends abruptly from a steep mountain slope onto a plain and deposits its load.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An alluvial fan is formed when a stream flowing down a steep gradient suddenly reaches a gentle plain. The abrupt fall in gradient causes a sharp loss of velocity and of carrying capacity, so the stream drops its load in a fan or cone-shaped spread at the foot of the slope. (जलोढ़ पंख — पर्वतपदीय निक्षेप)

 

• The coarser material is deposited nearest the mountain and the finer material further out. Where several fans coalesce along the foot of a range they form a continuous belt called a bajada.

 

• In India, alluvial fans are well developed along the foothills of the Himalayas, where the bhabar belt of coarse pebbly deposits gives way southwards to the marshy terai.

 

• Other landforms of river deposition include the floodplain, natural levees, point bars, the delta, meanders and oxbow lakes; landforms of river erosion include V-shaped valleys, gorges, canyons, waterfalls, potholes and river terraces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Natural levees are low, broad ridges of coarse sediment built along the banks of a river in its floodplain, deposited when the river overflows during floods and its velocity falls at the margins. They are characteristic of the lower course of large rivers, and can raise the channel above the surrounding plain — a familiar problem on the Kosi and the Hwang Ho.

 

• A river's course is divided into the upper (youthful) stage, dominated by vertical erosion, the middle (mature) stage, dominated by lateral erosion and transport, and the lower (old) stage, dominated by deposition.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: A triangular deposit at a river mouth is a delta.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Wind-piled sand forms dunes such as barchans and seifs, not alluvial fans.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Unsorted debris left at a glacier's snout is a terminal moraine.

question: Which of the following statements about the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup is correct?
option_1: India won the title by defeating South Africa in the final played at Barbados
option_2: India lost the final to Australia at Ahmedabad
option_3: The tournament was hosted solely by the West Indies
option_4: England retained the title by defeating Pakistan in the final
solution_text:
The correct answer is India won the title by defeating South Africa in the final played at Barbados.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup, defeating South Africa by 7 runs in the final played at the Kensington Oval, Bridgetown, Barbados, on 29 June 2024. (टी20 विश्व कप 2024 — भारत विजेता)

 

• The tournament was jointly hosted by the West Indies and the United States, and was the first ICC World Cup to be held partly in the USA. It was also the first edition to feature 20 teams.

 

• Virat Kohli was named Player of the Match in the final and Jasprit Bumrah Player of the Tournament. Rohit Sharma captained the side and Rahul Dravid was the head coach. India went through the tournament unbeaten.

 

• This was India's second T20 World Cup title, the first having been won in the inaugural edition of 2007 in South Africa, under M.S. Dhoni. It ended an ICC trophy drought of eleven years for India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other major ICC titles: the Cricket World Cup of 1983 under Kapil Dev and of 2011 under M.S. Dhoni, and the Champions Trophy of 2002 (shared) and 2013.

 

• In football, the 2023 Intercontinental Cup final was played at Bhubaneswar, where India defeated Lebanon 2-0 to win the title, with both goals scored by Sunil Chhetri.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: India lost the 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup final to Australia at Ahmedabad — a different tournament.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The 2024 T20 World Cup was co-hosted by the West Indies and the United States.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: England won the 2022 edition by beating Pakistan; they did not retain it in 2024.

question: Which of the following traditional textiles of India is the 'ikat' tie-and-dye weave of Odisha, also known as Bandha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sambalpuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sambalpuri saree of Odisha, traditionally called Bandha, is woven by the ikat technique, in which the yarn is tied and dyed before weaving, so that the pattern emerges from the threads themselves rather than being printed on the finished cloth. (संबलपुरी — ओडिशा की बंधा इकत बुनाई)

 

• Its characteristic motifs are the shankha (conch), chakra (wheel) and phula (flower), usually in red, black and white, drawn from the iconography of Lord Jagannath. It received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2010.

 

• The main weaving centres are Sambalpur, Bargarh, Sonepur and Boudh districts of western Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous Indian textile traditions:

◦ Pochampally (Telangana) — also an ikat weave, known as "Silk City" weaving; the village was recognised by the UN as a "Best Tourism Village"

◦ Patola (Patan, Gujarat) — the celebrated double ikat silk, in which both warp and weft are resist-dyed

◦ Bandhani (Gujarat and Rajasthan) — a tie-and-dye done on the finished fabric, not on the yarn

◦ Banarasi (Uttar Pradesh) — brocade silk with zari work

◦ Kanjeevaram (Tamil Nadu), Chanderi and Maheshwari (Madhya Pradesh), Muga silk (Assam), Phulkari (Punjab), Kalamkari (Andhra Pradesh) and Tanglia weaving (Gujarat)

 

• A Geographical Indication (GI) tag identifies goods as originating from a definite territory where a given quality or reputation is attributable to that origin. It is granted under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, and administered from the GI Registry at Chennai. India's first GI tag went to Darjeeling tea.

 

NOTE

 

• Pochampally (Option 1): An ikat weave, but of Telangana, not Odisha.

 

• Patola (Option 2): The double ikat silk of Patan in Gujarat.

 

• Bandhani (Option 3): A tie-and-dye of Gujarat and Rajasthan, in which the cloth itself, and not the yarn, is tied before dyeing.

question:
Which of the following is/are characteristic features of landforms produced along a coastline?

1. Sea caves, arches and stacks are produced by marine erosion of a headland.

2. A spit is a ridge of sand or shingle with one end joined to the land and the other projecting into the sea.

3. A lagoon is formed where a bar or barrier encloses a body of water along the coast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 all are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. (तटीय भू-आकृतियाँ)

 

• Statement 1 is correct. Waves attack the weaker rock of a headland and hollow out a sea cave. Caves cut from both sides may meet to form a sea arch; when the roof of the arch collapses, the seaward pillar left standing is a stack; and when the stack is worn down, a stump remains. Continued erosion leaves a wave-cut platform backed by a sea cliff.

 

• Statement 2 is correct. A spit is a long ridge of sand or shingle deposited by longshore drift, attached to the land at one end and projecting into the sea or across a bay at the other. When a spit grows right across a bay it becomes a bar, and when it joins an island to the mainland it is called a tombolo.

 

• Statement 3 is correct. A lagoon is the shallow body of water cut off from the open sea by a bar, barrier beach or coral reef. India's best-known examples are Chilika Lake in Odisha, the largest brackish-water lagoon in India, and Pulicat Lake on the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Landforms of wind erosion in deserts include mushroom rocks (gara), with a slender base and broad upper cap, mesas and buttes, which are flat-topped residual hills resembling table surfaces, inselbergs, standing as isolated rock remnants, together with yardangs, zeugen, ventifacts and deflation hollows.

 

• Coasts are classified as emergent, where the land has risen relative to the sea, as along the Coromandel coast, and submergent, where the sea has advanced, as along the western coast near Mumbai.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them omits at least one statement that is factually accurate.

question: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) successfully entered the orbit of Mars on which date?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24 September 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), or Mangalyaan, was launched on 5 November 2013 by a PSLV-C25, and successfully entered Martian orbit on 24 September 2014. (मंगलयान — 24 सितंबर 2014 को मंगल की कक्षा में प्रवेश)

 

• With this India became the first country in the world to reach Mars orbit on its very first attempt, and the fourth space agency to reach Mars, after Roscosmos, NASA and the European Space Agency. It also made India the first Asian country to do so.

 

• The mission was remarkable for its low cost, about Rs. 450 crore, and was designed for a life of six months but continued to send data for about eight years. It carried five payloads, including the Methane Sensor for Mars and the Mars Colour Camera.

 

• The image of Mangalyaan appears on the reverse of the Rs. 2,000 currency note issued in 2016.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key ISRO milestones and their dates:

◦ Aryabhata, India's first satellite — 19 April 1975

◦ Chandrayaan-1 launch — 22 October 2008; it confirmed the presence of water molecules on the Moon

◦ Chandrayaan-3 soft landing near the lunar south pole — 23 August 2023, now observed as National Space Day

◦ Aditya-L1 launch — 2 September 2023

◦ SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment) — India successfully completed the docking operation on 16 January 2025, becoming the fourth country after the USA, Russia and China to master space docking, a capability essential for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station and for future crewed missions

 

NOTE

 

• 5 November 2013 (Option 1): The launch date of Mangalyaan, not the date of Mars orbit insertion.

 

• 22 October 2008 (Option 3): The launch date of Chandrayaan-1.

 

• 14 July 2019 (Option 4): The launch date of Chandrayaan-2.

question: The Neyveli mines, which hold the largest lignite deposits in India, are located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Neyveli lignite mines, in Cuddalore district of Tamil Nadu, hold the largest lignite reserves in India. They are worked by NLC India Limited (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation), a public sector enterprise that also runs pithead thermal power stations there. (नेवेली — तमिलनाडु, भारत का सबसे बड़ा लिग्नाइट भंडार)

 

• Lignite is brown coal, a low-grade coal of about 40 to 55 per cent carbon, soft, with high moisture content. It is used chiefly for power generation, being burnt at the pithead because it is uneconomical to transport.

 

• The grades of coal in ascending order of carbon content and quality are:

◦ Peat — least carbon, high moisture, low heating capacity

◦ Lignite — brown coal, 40-55% carbon

◦ Bituminous — 60-80% carbon, the most widely used, popular for metallurgical purposes

◦ Anthracite — over 80% carbon, the highest quality, hard and black

 

• Other lignite deposits occur in Gujarat (Kachchh), Rajasthan (Barmer, Bikaner) and Jammu and Kashmir.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's main bituminous coal reserves lie in the rocks of the Gondwana system, chiefly in the valleys of the Damodar (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, Giridih), the Godavari (Singareni), the Mahanadi (Talcher, Korba) and the Son. The Damodar valley of the north-eastern plateau is the country's most important coalfield region.

 

• Tertiary coal, of lower carbon content, occurs in Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

 

• Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh are the leading coal-producing states, and Coal India Limited is the world's largest coal producer.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Has the Singareni coalfields in the Godavari valley, which yield bituminous coal, not the largest lignite deposits.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2) and Rajasthan (Option 3): Both have lignite deposits, at Kachchh and at Barmer and Bikaner respectively, but on a much smaller scale than Neyveli.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

Under Article 75 of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lok Sabha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 75(3) provides that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha). (अनुच्छेद 75(3) — मंत्रिपरिषद लोकसभा के प्रति सामूहिक रूप से उत्तरदायी)

 

• The principle of collective responsibility is the bedrock of the parliamentary system. It means that all ministers stand or fall together: a decision of the Cabinet binds every minister, who must either defend it publicly or resign. If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence, the entire Council of Ministers must resign, including ministers who are members of the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Individual responsibility is provided by Article 75(2), under which ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President — in practice, the President may remove a minister on the advice of the Prime Minister.

 

• Other provisions of Article 75: the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and other ministers are appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister; the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, must not exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha, a limit imposed by the 91st Amendment, 2003; and a minister who is not a member of either House for six consecutive months ceases to be a minister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The principle of collective responsibility was borrowed from the British parliamentary system, along with the ideas of a nominal head of state, the Speaker's office, and the rule of law.

 

• At the State level, Article 164 provides the corresponding rule: the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

 

• Under Article 312, Parliament may create a new All-India Service only if the Rajya Sabha first passes a resolution to that effect, supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting — a power that recognises the States' interest in such services.

 

NOTE

 

• The Rajya Sabha (Option 1): Cannot remove the Council of Ministers, since a no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.

 

• The President (Option 3): Individual ministers hold office during the President's pleasure, but collective responsibility runs to the Lok Sabha.

 

• The Supreme Court (Option 4): Exercises judicial review over government action, but the Council of Ministers is not politically answerable to it.

question:
Arrange the following stages of the Union Budget in Parliament in their correct order:

A) Presentation of the Budget

B) General discussion

C) Scrutiny by the Departmental Standing Committees

D) Passing of the Appropriation Bill
solution_text:
The correct answer is A - B - C - D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Union Budget passes through six stages in Parliament, in the following order: (केंद्रीय बजट की छह अवस्थाएँ)

◦ Presentation of the Budget — by the Finance Minister in the Lok Sabha, on 1 February, with a Budget speech; it is laid before the Rajya Sabha thereafter

◦ General discussion — held in both Houses on the Budget as a whole; no motion can be moved and the Budget is not put to vote at this stage

◦ Scrutiny by Departmental Standing Committees — the House is adjourned for a period during which the 24 departmentally related standing committees examine the demands for grants of the ministries and report back

◦ Voting on demands for grants — only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has no power here. Cut motions may be moved

◦ Passing of the Appropriation Bill — legalises the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India

◦ Passing of the Finance Bill — gives effect to the taxation proposals

 

• The Budget is presented under Article 112, where it is called the Annual Financial Statement. No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund except under an appropriation made by law.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Three kinds of cut motions may be moved at the voting stage: the Policy Cut (reduce the demand to Re. 1), the Economy Cut (reduce by a specified amount) and the Token Cut (reduce by Rs. 100, to air a specific grievance).

 

• A Vote on Account, under Article 116, allows the government to draw funds to meet expenditure for a part of the financial year until the Budget is passed.

 

• The Budget was advanced to 1 February from 2017, and the separate Railway Budget was merged with the general Budget in the same year.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 give incorrect sequences. The general discussion always precedes the detailed scrutiny by the standing committees, and the Appropriation Bill is passed only after the demands for grants have been voted.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 17.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 17 provides that "Untouchability" is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden, and that the enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law. (अनुच्छेद 17 — अस्पृश्यता का उन्मूलन)

 

• Article 17 is absolute and admits of no exception. It is available against private individuals as well as the State, which distinguishes it from most other Fundamental Rights.

 

• Parliament gave effect to it through the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, renamed in 1976 as the Protection of Civil Rights Act, and further through the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

 

• The Right to Equality comprises Articles 14 to 18:

◦ Article 14 — equality before the law and equal protection of the laws

◦ Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth

◦ Article 16 — equality of opportunity in matters of public employment

◦ Article 17 — abolition of untouchability

◦ Article 18 — abolition of titles

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term "untouchability" is not defined anywhere in the Constitution or in any statute; the Mysore High Court has held that it refers to the practice as it developed historically in India, and not to its literal sense.

 

• Under Article 18, the State may not confer any title except a military or academic distinction, and no citizen may accept a title from a foreign state. National awards such as the Bharat Ratna and the Padma awards are not titles and were held valid in Balaji Raghavan v. Union of India (1996), provided they are not used as prefixes or suffixes.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 15 (Option 1): Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth; it applies against the State and in respect of access to public places.

 

• Article 16 (Option 2): Guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment and permits reservation for backward classes.

 

• Article 18 (Option 4): Abolishes titles.

question: 'Mission Karmayogi', the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, is anchored in which ministry?
option_3: The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB), was approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2020 and is anchored in the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions. (मिशन कर्मयोगी — कार्मिक, लोक शिकायत एवं पेंशन मंत्रालय)

 

• Its aim is to shift civil service training from a rule-based to a role-based approach, building the right attitude, skills and knowledge in every officer and creating a workforce that is creative, constructive, imaginative, proactive, professional and technology-enabled.

 

• Its digital backbone is the iGOT Karmayogi platform, an online learning portal offering courses to civil servants at all levels. The programme is guided by a Prime Minister's Human Resource Council, and implemented through the Karmayogi Bharat, a Special Purpose Vehicle set up as a not-for-profit company.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Dak Karmayogi' is the e-learning platform launched by the Department of Posts (DoP), under the Ministry of Communications, to train its own personnel — including Gramin Dak Sevaks — in the spirit of Mission Karmayogi.

 

• The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions is under the direct charge of the Prime Minister. Its three departments are the Department of Personnel and Training, the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, and the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare.

 

• The premier training institution for the IAS is the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration at Mussoorie, and for the IPS the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy at Hyderabad.

 

NOTE

 

• The Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 1): Administers the Indian Police Service cadre matters and internal security, but not this programme.

 

• The Ministry of Education (Option 2): Handles school and higher education policy, not civil services training.

 

• The Ministry of Finance (Option 4): Deals with the Budget, taxation and expenditure.

question: Under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, the target for grid-connected solar power capacity by 2022 was revised in 2015 to which figure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100 GW.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission (JNNSM) was launched in January 2010 as one of the eight national missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC). Its original target was 20 GW of grid-connected solar power by 2022. (राष्ट्रीय सौर मिशन — 2015 में लक्ष्य बढ़ाकर 100 गीगावाट)

 

• In 2015 the Government revised the target fivefold, to 100 GW by 2022, comprising 60 GW of large and medium-scale grid-connected solar projects and 40 GW of rooftop solar.

 

• This 100 GW of solar formed part of the wider national target of 175 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2022 — 100 GW solar, 60 GW wind, 10 GW biomass and 5 GW small hydro.

 

• India's longer-term commitment, announced at COP-26 in Glasgow (2021), is 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel energy capacity by 2030, and net zero by 2070.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The nodal ministry is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). Key programmes include PM-KUSUM for solar pumps, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for rooftop solar in households, and the National Green Hydrogen Mission launched in 2023.

 

• Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan is among the largest solar parks in the world, and Pavagada in Karnataka is another very large installation.

 

• A key priority identified for energy transition worldwide is the modernisation and digitalisation of power grids and storage systems, since renewables are intermittent and need flexible grids and storage to be integrated at scale.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 GW (Option 1): The original target set in 2010, before the 2015 revision.

 

• 175 GW (Option 3): The target for total renewable energy capacity by 2022, of which solar was 100 GW.

 

• 450 GW (Option 4): An intermediate announcement for renewable capacity by 2030, later raised to 500 GW of non-fossil capacity at COP-26.

question: The folk dance 'Hojagiri', in which women dance while balancing on an earthen pitcher with a bottle and lamp on the head, belongs to which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hojagiri is the best-known folk dance of Tripura, performed by the women of the Reang (Bru) community. (होजागिरी — त्रिपुरा का लोक नृत्य)

 

• Its distinguishing feature is the extraordinary balance it demands: the dancers stand on an earthen pitcher, balance a bottle on the head with a lighted lamp on it, and move the lower half of the body while the upper half remains still, often with a handkerchief or plate in the hands.

 

• It is performed during the Laxmi Puja festival, held on the full moon night after Durga Puja, and the name is derived from the invocation to the goddess. The dance is accompanied by the kham (drum) and the sumui (flute).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Folk dances of the North East and neighbouring states:

◦ Manipur — Thang-Ta (martial dance), Lai Haraoba, Dhol Cholom

◦ Mizoram — Cheraw (bamboo dance), Khuallam

◦ Sikkim — Singhi Chham (snow lion dance), Maruni

◦ Assam — Bihu, Bagurumba

◦ Meghalaya — Nongkrem, Wangala, Shad Suk Mynsiem

◦ Nagaland — Chang Lo (Sua Lua), Zeliang

 

• Some southern and western folk dances: Dollu Kunitha, performed with large drums slung around the neck, belongs to Karnataka; Kolattam and Kuchipudi's folk antecedents to Andhra Pradesh; Lavani to Maharashtra; and Garba to Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for Thang-Ta and the classical Manipuri dance.

 

• Mizoram (Option 2): Known for Cheraw, the bamboo dance.

 

• Sikkim (Option 3): Known for Singhi Chham, the snow lion dance.

question: 'Mission LiFE', launched by India, is aimed primarily at which of the following?
option_1: Financing large hydroelectric projects in the Himalayan states
option_2: Promoting individual and community pro-environment behaviour and mindful consumption
option_3: Creating a compliance carbon market for heavy industry
option_4: Establishing wildlife corridors between protected areas
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promoting individual and community pro-environment behaviour and mindful consumption.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mission LiFE — Lifestyle for Environment was announced by India at COP-26 in Glasgow (2021) and formally launched in October 2022 at Kevadia, Gujarat. It seeks to shift the world from "mindless and destructive consumption" to "mindful and deliberate utilisation". (मिशन लाइफ — पर्यावरण के लिए जीवन शैली)

 

• Its central idea is that individual and community behaviour, and not government policy alone, is decisive for climate action. It promotes simple everyday actions such as saving energy and water, reducing single-use plastic, adopting sustainable food systems, reducing waste, adopting healthy lifestyles and e-waste management — seven themes in all.

 

• The Mission works through a strategy of Change in Demand, Change in Supply and Change in Policy, and is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Its message is carried by the idea of the "Pro-Planet People (P3)".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Credit Programme, notified in 2023 and rolled out from 2024, is a distinct market-based mechanism that incentivises voluntary environmental action — such as tree plantation, water conservation and waste management — by awarding tradable green credits to individuals, industries and local bodies. Its main goal is to encourage eco-restoration through credit incentives.

 

• India's other climate commitments under its updated Nationally Determined Contributions include reducing the emissions intensity of GDP by 45 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030 and creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Hydropower financing is handled through separate schemes of the Ministry of Power, not Mission LiFE.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: A carbon market is being developed under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023, framed under the Energy Conservation Act — a different instrument.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Wildlife corridors fall under Project Tiger, Project Elephant and the work of the National Board for Wildlife.

question:
Which of the following statements about the sugar industry in India is/are correct?

1. India is among the largest producers of sugarcane in the world.

2. Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are the leading sugar-producing states.

3. It is a seasonal industry, well suited to the cooperative sector.

4. Sugar mills are located near consuming centres rather than near the cane fields.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. India is among the largest producers of sugarcane and of sugar in the world, rivalling Brazil, and sugar is the country's second largest agro-based industry after cotton textiles. (गन्ना उत्पादन — भारत विश्व में अग्रणी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra together account for the bulk of India's sugar output. The industry has been shifting steadily southwards, to Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, because the cane grown there has a higher sucrose content, the crushing season is longer, and the cooperative sector is better organised.

 

• Statement 3 is correct. Sugar is a seasonal industry, working only during the crushing season of about four to seven months. This makes it ideally suited to the cooperative sector, and the cooperative sugar mills of Maharashtra are the classic Indian example of cooperative-sector industry.

 

• Statement 4 is incorrect. Sugar mills are located close to the cane-growing areas, not near consuming centres. Sugarcane is a bulky, weight-losing raw material whose sucrose content begins to fall within 24 hours of harvesting, so the cane must be crushed as soon as possible after cutting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major problems of the industry include the short crushing season, fluctuating cane production, low sucrose content of the cane grown in the north, obsolete machinery in older mills, and delayed payment of cane arrears to farmers.

 

• By-products of sugar manufacture are bagasse, used for paper and as fuel, and molasses, used to produce ethanol — which links the industry to the Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme.

 

• In the fertilizer industry, by contrast, urea is the most commonly produced nitrogenous fertilizer, production expanded greatly after the Green Revolution, and Gujarat is in fact a leading producer — while India remains wholly dependent on imports for potash, since it has no commercially viable potash reserves.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect. Options 2 and 4 include Statement 4, which reverses the true locational logic of the industry, and Option 1 omits Statement 2, which is factually accurate.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ramsar Convention:

1. It is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.

2. It was signed in 1971 in the Iranian city of Ramsar.

3. India's first two Ramsar sites were Chilika Lake and Loktak Lake.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Ramsar Convention is an intergovernmental treaty providing the framework for the conservation and wise use of wetlands and their resources. (रामसर अभिसमय — आर्द्रभूमि संरक्षण)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. It was signed on 2 February 1971 in the Iranian city of Ramsar, on the shores of the Caspian Sea, and came into force in 1975. 2 February is observed every year as World Wetlands Day.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect. India became a party to the Convention in 1982, and its first two Ramsar sites, both designated in 1981, were Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Keoladeo National Park (Bharatpur, Rajasthan) — not Loktak Lake. Loktak Lake in Manipur, famous for its floating phumdis and the Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world, was designated later, in 1990.

 

• A wetland is placed on the Montreux Record when its ecological character has changed or is likely to change. India's sites on that record are Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake; Chilika was placed on it and later removed after successful restoration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has well over 80 Ramsar sites, the largest number in Asia, covering the greatest area of any country in the continent. Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh have the most sites among the states.

 

• Chilika Lake is the largest brackish-water lagoon in India and a winter home for migratory birds; Sundarbans is the largest Ramsar site in India by area.

 

• Wetlands are valued as the "kidneys of the landscape", for groundwater recharge, flood control, water purification, carbon storage and as habitat for migratory birds.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each of them includes Statement 3, which misnames India's first Ramsar sites. The correct pair is Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park, both designated in 1981.

question: The 'Sarhul' festival, celebrated by the tribal communities of Jharkhand, marks which of the following?
option_1: The harvest of paddy at the end of the monsoon
option_2: A ritual observed in mourning for departed ancestors
option_3: The taming of cattle before the ploughing season
option_4: The worship of the Sal tree and the beginning of the new year with the blossoming of sal flowers
solution_text:
The correct answer is The worship of the Sal tree and the beginning of the new year with the blossoming of sal flowers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sarhul is the principal spring festival of the Oraon, Munda, Ho and Santhal communities of Jharkhand and adjoining areas. Its name means "worship of the Sal tree", and it is celebrated when the sal tree blossoms, in the month of Chaitra (March-April). (सरहुल — साल वृक्ष की पूजा, नववर्ष का आरंभ)

 

• It marks the beginning of the new year for these communities and is understood as the symbolic marriage of the Sun (Dharmesh) and the Earth (Dharti Ayo), in which the earth becomes fertile and ready for cultivation.

 

• The rituals are conducted by the village priest, the Pahan, in the sacred grove called the Sarna sthal, and no ploughing or sowing may begin until the festival is over. It is accompanied by the Sarhul dance and the drinking of rice beer (*handia*).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other festivals of Jharkhand and its tribal communities:

◦ Karma — worship of the karam tree, observed for the wellbeing of brothers

◦ Jawa — associated with Karma, in which unmarried girls sow grain in baskets and offer green melons, a rite symbolising the desire for a son and for fertility

◦ Sohrai — the cattle festival, celebrated around Diwali, known for its wall paintings

◦ Tusu Parab — a harvest festival of the Chotanagpur region, held at Makar Sankranti

 

• The Sarna religion, based on nature worship centred on the sacred grove, is followed by a large number of tribal people in Jharkhand, and a demand for its separate recognition in the Census has long been raised.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The autumn harvest is marked by festivals such as Sohrai and Tusu, not Sarhul.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Sarhul is a festival of renewal and fertility, not of mourning.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Cattle are honoured at Sohrai, the cattle festival celebrated around Diwali.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. The National Development Council was a constitutional body established under Article 263.

2. The NITI Aayog was established in 2015 by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is incorrect. The National Development Council (NDC), set up in 1952, was neither a constitutional nor a statutory body. It was created by an executive resolution of the Government of India and is described as an extra-constitutional and extra-legal body. (राष्ट्रीय विकास परिषद — संवैधानिक निकाय नहीं)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The NITI Aayog — the National Institution for Transforming India — was established on 1 January 2015 by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet, replacing the Planning Commission, which had itself been set up by a resolution in 1950.

 

• The NDC was chaired by the Prime Minister, with all Union Cabinet Ministers, the Chief Ministers of all States, the administrators of Union Territories and the members of the Planning Commission as members. Its function was to approve the Five Year Plans.

 

• The NITI Aayog is chaired by the Prime Minister, and has a Vice-Chairperson, full-time members, ex-officio members, special invitees, and a Governing Council comprising all Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors. It acts as a think tank and advisory body promoting cooperative and competitive federalism, and unlike the Planning Commission it does not allocate funds to the States.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• By contrast, the Inter-State Council is provided for in the Constitution, under Article 263, under which the President may establish it if it appears to him that the public interest would be served. It was actually set up in 1990, on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission. Its recommendations, however, are advisory and not binding.

 

• Bodies are classified as constitutional (Election Commission, CAG, Finance Commission, UPSC), statutory (NHRC, NGT, NCW, Lokpal, SEBI, NADA) and executive or non-statutory (NITI Aayog, the erstwhile Planning Commission and NDC, the Central Vigilance Commission before 2003).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each of them misstates the position of at least one body. The commonest error is to assume that the NDC, being so important in the planning process, must have had constitutional standing — it did not.

question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option.

Assertion (A): ISRO is developing the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) to succeed the LVM3 for heavy payload missions.

Reason (R): The NGLV is being designed as a partially reusable vehicle with a substantially greater payload capacity to Low Earth Orbit than the LVM3.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. ISRO is developing the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV), also referred to as Soorya, as the successor to the LVM3 for India's future heavy-lift requirements, including the Bharatiya Antariksh Station and crewed lunar missions. (एनजीएलवी — अगली पीढ़ी का प्रक्षेपण यान)

 

• Reason (R) is true. The NGLV is being designed as a partially reusable three-stage vehicle using semi-cryogenic propulsion with LOX-methane in the upper stages, and is intended to carry roughly 30 tonnes to Low Earth Orbit — about three times the LVM3's capacity — at a significantly lower cost per kilogram.

 

• R correctly explains A. The very reason a successor to the LVM3 is required is that India's planned missions demand far heavier payloads at lower cost than the existing vehicle can deliver. The design features stated in R — reusability and a threefold payload capacity — are precisely why the NGLV is being developed as the successor. R therefore supplies the cause, not merely an additional fact.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A Third Launch Pad (TLP) is being developed at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (SDSC-SHAR), specifically to raise India's launch frequency and to accommodate larger next-generation vehicles such as the NGLV. A second spaceport for small launchers is coming up at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu.

 

• ISRO's current operational fleet comprises the PSLV, the GSLV Mk II, the LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) and the SSLV. The RLV-TD (Pushpak) is the technology demonstrator for reusable launch vehicles.

 

• The Indian Space Policy 2023 opened the sector to private participation, with IN-SPACe as the regulator and promoter and NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) as the commercial arm of ISRO.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: R is not an unrelated fact; the payload and reusability requirements are the reason the new vehicle is being built.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.
